trace.answer: Your VCs Are Worried About Public Multiples. Do You Need To Worry, Too? There’s no shortage of data on how public multiples have compressed across SaaS companies over the past two years—MSCI reports revenue multiples for B2B software stocks fell nearly 50% since Q4’22 while enterprise value multiples dropped by roughly half from 23x to around 11x. But here’s what matters more than any headline metric: your company isn’t public yet. What this means is you don’t need to model your business off public market valuations. The reality is most private markets investors won’t even look at you based solely on multiple comparisons with public comps anyway. They’re going to evaluate your fundamentals first and foremost. If your business shows clear signs of strong execution, solid unit economics, and growing competitive advantages, you’ll likely attract investment regardless of where your multiple sits relative to the public market median. As one investor put it, “The good news for startups is there is still room for high growth and high quality companies to get funded.” So if you're worried about being impacted by declining public multiples, remember that your valuation will depend much more heavily on your internal fundamentals than external market conditions.
